name: Grafana Labs (formerly Raintank)
origin_detail: Torkel Ödegaard created Grafana in 2013 as a dashboard project derived from Kibana 3. Raj Dutt's New York startup Raintank (2014) built its business on Grafana, brought Ödegaard in as a co-founder and renamed itself Grafana Labs.
openness_notes: Grafana began as Apache-2.0. In 2021 Grafana, Loki and Tempo moved to AGPL-3.0, which is still OSI-approved, while some agents and libraries stayed Apache-2.0. Revenue comes from Grafana Cloud and proprietary Grafana Enterprise features, so the current level is open core (2).

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Copyleft tightening that stayed within OSI licences, aimed at hosted resale; no significant fork known (unverified)

robustness: Single-vendor, VC-backed, but the projects remain OSI-licensed (AGPL), so a fork stays legally possible.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. Grafana Labs is the main counter-example to SSPL/BSL relicensing in this group: it tightened to AGPL in 2021, kept the open-source label, and kept raising venture money at rising valuations. Valuation, funding and revenue need sourcing.
